provenance.basis: The new tax regime for FY2025-26, unchanged for FY2026-27 per several secondary sources (bank and tax-site explainers, not the Finance Act itself): nothing up to 4 lakh, then 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25% and 30% above 24 lakh; standard deduction 75,000 for salary; no tax at all if taxable income is up to 12 lakh (section 87A rebate), with marginal relief just above it. Cess 4%. Surcharge tiers (10% above 50 lakh, 15% above 1 crore, 25% above 2 crore) are from memory and were not confirmed in this pass; relief at the surcharge thresholds is ignored. Only the new regime is modelled (no 80C, HRA or home-loan deductions). The slabs are assumed to rise with prices (they have risen about 4-5% a year, roughly with inflation), so a rupee of real income is taxed the same in any year.
PPF interest is tax-free; EPF interest is tax-free up to a yearly contribution limit that is ignored here.
Bank deposit interest is taxed as ordinary income every year as it builds up, at your slab rate, whether or not you withdraw it. Savings-account interest is treated the same way.

Equity funds and listed shares: gains on holdings sold after more than 12 months are taxed at 12.5% beyond 1.25 lakh a year; sold sooner, at 20%. Rates in force since July 2024 and still current for FY2026-27 per several secondary sources. Sales happen at year end in this game, so a holding kept exactly one year counts as long-term. The exemption is assumed to rise with prices. Losses are not carried forward.

Physical gold: gains on holdings sold after more than 24 months are taxed at 12.5% without indexation; sold sooner, the gain is added to income and taxed at your slab rate. Sources disagreed on the period for gold ETFs (12 or 24 months); the 24-month rule is used. Sales happen at year end, so a holding kept exactly two years counts as long-term.

Selling a home: gains after more than 24 months are taxed at 12.5% without indexation (the rate for long-term assets other than shares, per secondary sources); sooner, at your slab rate. Only relevant when the game sells your home as a last resort. Exemptions for reinvesting in another home, and the older indexation option for homes bought before July 2024, are ignored.

Illustrative, rounded and simplified: the amount you pay is worked out once a year from your pay, interest and the gains you realised. Tax on gains you have not yet sold is not counted, so net worth before retirement is before that tax.
